question: What do I check before starting a new fire pump drive engine for the first time?
reference_answer: Before operating, complete the safety checks, remove tools and foreign objects, make sure the guards are in place and tell the people nearby. Then inspect: (1) no apparent damage and all components fitted; (2) the drive belt is properly installed; (3) hoses and tubes are properly installed; (4) electrical connections are properly installed; (5) the engine is installed to the pump maker's instructions, aligned and free to rotate; (6) the grease fittings on the auxiliary drive shaft are lubricated.

question: How do I do the weekly battery maintenance?
reference_answer: Wear gloves and eye protection. (1) Keep the batteries clean by wiping with a damp cloth. (2) Check the specific gravity of each cell with a hydrometer: a full battery reads 1.260 and a battery below 1.215 is replaced. (3) Check the wiring and cable connections for loose, corroded, worn or damaged cables. Clean corroded clamps, negative cable first, with emery cloth or a wire brush, wash the terminals with baking soda and water, flush with clean water, coat with petroleum jelly, reinstall and tighten. (4) Check the electrolyte level monthly and fill with distilled water to the bottom of the filler neck. (5) Check continuity between terminals and the insulation resistance to ground. (6) Reinstall the cables and attach the negative cable last.

question: How is the drive shaft lubricated?
reference_answer: (1) Remove the drive shaft guards. (2) Wipe the grease fittings and the grease gun nozzle with a clean cloth. (3) Add grease to the universal joint grease fittings. (4) Wipe excess grease from the fittings.

question: How do I remove and reinstall the coolant thermostat?
reference_answer: Use the correct thermostat and never run the engine without one. (1) Remove the upper coolant hose clamps and the upper coolant hose at the thermostat housing. (2) Remove the two thermostat housing flange cap screws and the flange. (3) Remove the thermostat and gasket. (4) Clean dirt, oxidation and sludge from the flange faces. (5) If the thermostat is still good, reinstall it. Inspect the seal on the flange and apply a new seal if it is damaged or cracked. (6) Replace the thermostat flange and cap screws.

question: How do I start and stop the engine locally at the digital panel?
reference_answer: To start: (1) press the AUTO/MAN selector switch to put the engine in manual mode; (2) press CRANK BATT A and/or CRANK BATT B to crank. To stop: press the RESET/STOP switch, or press and hold the red Engine STOP button on the left of the panel.

question: The speed of my electronic fixed-speed engine does not match the factory setting plate. How do I adjust it?
reference_answer: On electronic engines only. (1) Press the ECM A selector switch. (2) Press MENU. (3) Press RPM ADJUSTMENT. (4) Press INC or DEC to change the ECM setpoint (10 RPM per press, not beyond 50 RPM either way). (5) Press RETURN. (6) Press the RESET/STOP switch and wait thirty seconds. (7) Repeat for ECM B. Never switch from ECM A to ECM B while the engine is running.

question: What fuel does the engine use?
reference_answer: Only no. 2 diesel fuel (ASTM no. 2D). Other fuel may affect emissions, and adjustments to make up for an alternative fuel are not warrantable.

question: At the first start the gauge shows no oil pressure, or the low oil pressure message appears within fifteen seconds. What do I do?
reference_answer: Stop the engine immediately. Continued operation without proper lubrication damages the engine.

question: The engine did not start automatically in a fire emergency. How do I start it by hand?
reference_answer: (1) Open the water bypass valves in the cooling water supply, or the emergency cooling supply. (2) Press the AUTO/MAN switch to put the engine in manual mode. (3) Open the panel door, slide the key switch override to the right and check that LED 49 KEY FB is lit. Do not crank for more than fifteen seconds, wait fifteen seconds between attempts, up to six attempts. (4) Press down on the Battery A or the Battery B contactor lever. If A does not engage the starter, use B; if the batteries are weak, press both together. Release the lever as soon as the engine starts. If it has not started after three attempts, check the fuel supply: no blue or white exhaust smoke while cranking means no fuel is delivered. (5) Check that the engine runs at rated speed and shows oil pressure within fifteen seconds.

question: How do I do the weekly test run and what do I check during it?
reference_answer: Start the engine at least once a week and run it for at least thirty minutes with as much load as possible. During the run check: (1) oil pressure shows within fifteen seconds of starting; (2) the engine reaches normal running temperature after thirty minutes; (3) it runs at the proper speed (if not, see the engine operation checks); (4) no unusual noise; (5) oil pressure is above 69 kPa (10 psi); (6) coolant temperature is between 70 and 107 °C (158 and 225 °F); (7) both battery voltmeters show 12 VDC (24 VDC on the optional system); (8) the air filter indicator has not popped up. End the run by pressing and holding the RESET/STOP switch until the engine stops.

question: How do I change the engine oil and filter?
reference_answer: Do it at least once a year. (1) Run the engine until the coolant is at 70 °C (158 °F), then shut it off. (2) Put a container under the drain plug. (3) Remove the plug and drain the oil. (4) Remove the filter: clean around it, use a filter wrench, discard the O-ring if it stayed on the flange, clean the flange and put a light film of 15W-40 on the new gasket. (5) Fill the new filter with 15W-40. (6) Screw it on until the gasket is snug and add a quarter turn. (7) Clean the drain plug threads, refit and torque the plug. (8) Fill to the proper level; if there is no oil pressure within fifteen seconds of starting, shut down. (9) Run the engine one to two minutes. (10) Stop it. (11) Wait about fifteen minutes. (12) Check the level and top up to the H mark.

question: How is the heat exchanger pressure tested when an internal leak is suspected, and what if it leaks?
reference_answer: Apply air pressure of 276 kPa (40 psi) with a 689 kPa (100 psi) gauge at the cooling water inlet, isolate the source and watch the gauge for five minutes. The pressure must not change. If leakage is found, the heat exchanger must be replaced.

question: How do I change the fuel filters, and what if the engine does not restart?
reference_answer: (1) Shut off the engine. (2) Close any fuel valves. (3) Clean around the filter or separator heads. (4) Remove the spent canisters with a filter wrench. (5) Clean the mounting head surfaces of sludge. (6) Lubricate the gasket seals with clean 15W-40. (7) Screw the canister on until the gasket is snug and add a quarter turn. (8) Open the fuel supply valves. (9) Press CRANK BATT A or B to start the engine. (10) Hold the contactor for up to fifteen seconds or until it starts, and repeat up to three times. If it has not started after three attempts, check the fuel supply system.

question: How do I run the overspeed test from the panel, and what happens at the end?
reference_answer: (1) Press MENU. (2) Press OVERSPEED TEST. (3) If needed, press RPM ADJUSTMENT and use INC and DEC to change the speed in steps of ten RPM. (4) Press RUN. (5) A dialog warns that the engine will ramp to overspeed. If it is safe, select Yes; if not, select No. (6) When the timer expires, ENGINE OVERSPEED flashes in red at the top of the screen. (7) The engine goes to manual mode until reset. (8) Press the RESET/STOP switch to reset it.

question: I held the Engine STOP button until the engine stopped, let go, and the engine started again. Why?
reference_answer: When the button is released the engine tries to restart if the fire pump controller still sends a pump-on-demand signal. The engine must also be stopped at the fire pump controller.

question: The coolant gauge on the panel has gone yellow and the engine is cold, below 100 °F. Is something wrong?
reference_answer: Yellow below 100 °F (38 °C) comes with a low coolant temperature fault (low engine temperature, TB-312). The gauge is also yellow between 200 and 211 °F (93 and 100 °C).

question: What pressure are the cooling loop water pressure regulators set to on a CFP60E?
reference_answer: 345 kPa (50 psi). The CFP30E, CFP50 and CFP60E use 345 kPa (50 psi). The CFP5E to CFP23E use 276 kPa (40 psi).

question: My engine is radiator-cooled. Do the raw water high inlet temperature and clogged strainer signals apply to it?
reference_answer: No. TB-310 (raw water high inlet temperature) and TB-311 (clogged raw water cooling loop strainer) are not applicable on radiator-cooled models.

reference_answer: The manual gives no valve lash values. It recommends valve lash maintenance every four years by a skilled technician.

question: What is the maximum axial end-play allowed on the turbocharger shaft?

question: What is the total engine oil system capacity of a CFP23E?
reference_answer: The manual gives no oil capacity for the CFP23E. The engine data section (page 111, section 7.4) says its data pages are for the CFP11E. The data page itself (page 112) does not name the model. The CFP23E appears elsewhere only in model lists, the regulator pressure note, the oil level gauge note, the overspeed rating list and the minimum crank speed table.

question: Which spare parts should I keep in stock for this engine?

question: What flow rate in gpm does the fire pump itself deliver?

question: Which lubricating oil filter is recommended for the CFP11E?
